label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
Our Winter School on Elliptic Curves and Modular Forms wrapped up on Saturday, and I'm still a bit tired and very happy. Here are a few thank-yous on behalf of the organising team.

From 5 to 7 November, 41 MSc and early PhD students from 9 states spent three days in Seminar Hall 2, Department of Mathematics, Sahyadri Institute of Science, Pune. We received 112 applications and selected participants based on a statement of purpose and one reference letter. A Rs 2.4 lakh grant from the institute's student initiative fund covered hostel stay and travel for 18 outstation students.

Thank you to our speakers:
Dr. Nilesh Dharmadhikari (Hyderabad), for his lectures on the Mordell-Weil theorem
Dr. Sunanda Iyer (Chennai), for her lectures on modular forms
Dr. Tomasz Wierzbicki, who joined online from Kraków to take us through computations in Sage

One moment I'll remember: an MSc student from Silchar spotted an error in a worked example in Dr. Iyer's notes. She corrected it live and thanked him in front of everyone. That's exactly the kind of exchange we were hoping for.

Thank you to Prof. Anuradha Venkatesan, our faculty mentor, for her guidance and support throughout.

Thank you to Mr. Prakash Salunke from the department office, who sorted out hostel rooms at 11 pm when a booking got messed up. We'd have been in real trouble without him.

Thank you to the six PhD students who did TA work and ran the problem sessions. That format worked really well, and we're keeping it.

Thank you to my co-organisers Ketaki Joglekar and Faizan Mirza. Three days of running around, and we're somehow still friends.

And thank you to every participant. On day 2 the power went out for nearly two hours and all the laptops died. We moved the problem session to the canteen with two rolling whiteboards, and it turned out to be the best session of the three days.

If there's one thing I'm taking away, it's that small schools like this matter more for MSc students than big conferences do. In a room of 41, people actually get to ask their questions.

Slides and problem sheets will go up on the department website within two weeks. I'll share the link here once they're live.

We hope to run a second edition in late 2027, depending on grant funding. Fingers crossed!

#Mathematics #NumberTheory #EllipticCurves #ModularForms #WinterSchool
